what_it_does: IBM's Telum II is the latest enterprise server processor, a microchip that runs the financial and corporate software stack at 5.5 billion cycles per second across 8 parallel cores. This new generation extends the previous Telum design with three major upgrades: a dedicated Data Processing Unit (new hardware specifically built to accelerate artificial intelligence calculations), 40 percent more high-speed cache memory (the closest, fastest memory adjacent to the processing cores), and better branch prediction (guessing which instruction path the program will take next). The chip contains 43 billion transistors packed into a space the size of a postage stamp and can be linked together (up to 32 chips) for the largest deployments, keeping data coherent across the whole system.
